summary: California's Point Pinos Light, lit in 1855 at the mouth of Monterey Bay, kept by a widow who took over from her shot husband and later by the 'Socialite Keeper' Emily Fish.

structures.material: brick, rebuilt in reinforced concrete after 1906

access.note: City of Pacific Grove museum with limited weekly hours; Coast Guard keeps the light.

notes_for_editor: Sources differ on: Layton's death year (1855 per the Alta and Heritage Society, 1856 per the city page), Charlotte Layton's start (1855 USLHS vs 4 Jan 1856 Heritage Society), the 1906 tower damage (top 5 ft per Lighthouse Friends; torn down per Putnam; rebuilt 1907 per NRHP), kerosene date (1882 city vs 1883 LHF). Lighthouse Friends lists a keeper James E. Lucas (1960) not in the USLHS roster; roster follows the USLHS page (laborer lines added at fact-check); the USCG crew lines (1960-1969, living-people rule) and William H. Kimball (USCG, to 1946) were not added. 'climbable' removed (no source). NRHP text is OCR with garbled columns. No Chronicling America hits found for Point Pinos/Emily Fish. Commissioner 1915 hit sits in a bound volume of several reports; page cited from corpus (printed p.87). Alta letter is cited via the Heritage Society transcription, not read at loc.gov or CDNC.
